abbrev Word32 := BitVec 32
abbrev Word64 := BitVec 64

abbrev Buffers := Argument → Word64

structure TensorData (layout : Layout) (rows : Nat) where
  weights : Fin rows → Fin layout.inputWidth → FP32.Bits
  input : Fin layout.inputWidth → FP32.Bits
  bias : Fin rows → FP32.Bits

/-- Addresses retain byte units even though memory stores complete FP32 words. -/
def weightAddress (layout : Layout) (buffers : Buffers) (i j : Nat) : Word64 :=
  buffers .weights + BitVec.ofNat 64 (i * layout.rowStride + j * fp32Bytes)

def elementAddress (buffers : Buffers) (arg : Argument) (i : Nat) : Word64 :=
  buffers arg + BitVec.ofNat 64 (i * fp32Bytes)

from.quote:
The input memory contains the supplied weight, input, and bias words at their
computed addresses. The single-thread theorem requires no output separation:
all input reads finish before its only store. Exactly the selected output word
is updated, and every other address keeps its initial contents. Read-only
inputs may overlap when their specified values agree. No initial contents are
required for a separate output location.

`OutputsSeparated` is an optional launch-level contract excluding output/input
and output/output overlap. It is retained for composing different threads,
and is not a hypothesis of the single-thread theorem.

passage.quote:
/-- Correct input words at the addresses used by the computation. -/
structure InputsStored (layout : Layout) (rows : Nat) (buffers : Buffers)
    (data : TensorData layout rows) (memory : GlobalMemory) : Prop where
  weights : ∀ i j, memory (weightAddress layout buffers i.val j.val) = some (data.weights i j)
  input : ∀ j, memory (elementAddress buffers .input j.val) = some (data.input j)
  bias : ∀ i, memory (elementAddress buffers .bias i.val) = some (data.bias i)

/-- Optional launch-level separation; single-thread correctness does not require it. -/
structure OutputsSeparated (layout : Layout) (rows : Nat) (buffers : Buffers) : Prop where
  weights : ∀ (i r : Fin rows) (j : Fin layout.inputWidth),
    elementAddress buffers .output i.val ≠ weightAddress layout buffers r.val j.val
  input : ∀ (i : Fin rows) (j : Fin layout.inputWidth),
    elementAddress buffers .output i.val ≠ elementAddress buffers .input j.val
  bias : ∀ (i r : Fin rows),
    elementAddress buffers .output i.val ≠ elementAddress buffers .bias r.val
  outputs : ∀ (i r : Fin rows), i ≠ r →
    elementAddress buffers .output i.val ≠ elementAddress buffers .output r.val

The maximum with positive zero is defined directly from binary32 sign, exponent,
and fraction bits. It maps NaNs and negative values, including negative zero,
to positive zero, preserves positive infinity and positive subnormal values,
and leaves positive zero unchanged. This follows the selected unmodified
[`max.f32` rule](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/12.0.1/parallel-thread-execution/index.html#floating-point-instructions-max).

passage.quote:
/-- Binary32 storage, retaining signed zeros, infinities and NaN payloads. -/
abbrev Bits := Word32

def positiveZero : Bits := 0
def fractionBits : Nat := 23
def exponentBits : Nat := 8

def fraction (v : Bits) : Nat := v.toNat % 2 ^ fractionBits
def exponent (v : Bits) : Nat := v.toNat / 2 ^ fractionBits % 2 ^ exponentBits
def negative (v : Bits) : Bool := decide (2 ^ (fractionBits + exponentBits) ≤ v.toNat)
def isNaN (v : Bits) : Bool :=
  decide (exponent v = 2 ^ exponentBits - 1 ∧ fraction v ≠ 0)

/-- The selected max.f32 with a fixed positive-zero second operand, without .ftz. -/
def maxPositiveZero (v : Bits) : Bits :=
  if isNaN v || negative v then positiveZero else v

from.quote:
The ordered result starts from positive zero and folds an FMA over columns
`0` through `n - 1`, then performs one bias addition and a maximum with positive
zero. The prefix accumulator records the same fold over the first `k` columns:

passage.quote:
/-- Column order is carried by Fin enumeration, not an unordered sum. -/
def rowTerms (data : TensorData layout rows) (i : Fin rows) : List (FP32.Bits × FP32.Bits) :=
  List.ofFn (fun j => (data.weights i j, data.input j))

/-- First k FMA updates from positive zero, using the supplied arithmetic operations. -/
def prefixAccumulator (ops : FP32.Arithmetic) (data : TensorData layout rows)
    (i : Fin rows) (k : Nat) : FP32.Bits :=
  ((rowTerms data i).take k).foldl
    (fun acc term => ops.fmaRN term.1 term.2 acc) FP32.positiveZero

@[simp] theorem prefixAccumulator_zero (ops : FP32.Arithmetic)
    (data : TensorData layout rows) (i : Fin rows) :
    prefixAccumulator ops data i 0 = FP32.positiveZero := by
  simp [prefixAccumulator]

def rowResult (ops : FP32.Arithmetic) (data : TensorData layout rows) (i : Fin rows) : FP32.Bits :=
  FP32.maxPositiveZero (ops.addRN (prefixAccumulator ops data i layout.inputWidth) (data.bias i))

/-- Entry to the independent fragment at PTX line 43; scratch contents are unrestricted. -/
structure BodyEntry (layout : Layout) (rows : Nat)
    (buffers : Buffers) (data : TensorData layout rows)
    (i : Fin rows) (initial : State Register) : Prop where
  inputs : InputsStored layout rows buffers data initial.globalMemory
  pc : initial.pc = 0
  active : initial.returned = false
  row : (initial.regs .row).toNat = i.val
  weightRead : initial.regs64 .weightRead = weightAddress layout buffers i.val 0
  inputRead : initial.regs64 .inputRead = buffers .input
  biasRead : initial.regs64 .biasRead = elementAddress buffers .bias i.val
  outputWrite : initial.regs64 .outputWrite = elementAddress buffers .output i.val

loop execution is unchanged by the appended instructions; its final PC points
to the suffix. The suffix theorem applies at that offset, using the loop's

passage.quote:
/-- Block four: initialized dot loop followed by bias/ReLU/store/return. -/
def bodyProgram (width : Nat) : List (Instruction Register) := dotLoop width ++ reluSuffix

def bodySteps (width : Nat) : Nat := dotLoopStart + dotIterationSteps * width + reluSuffix.length

/-- The complete computational block returns with the specified output and preserved frame. -/
structure BodyResult (ops : FP32.Arithmetic) (data : TensorData layout rows)
    (buffers : Buffers) (i : Fin rows) (initial final : State Register) : Prop where
  pc : final.pc = (bodyProgram layout.inputWidth).length
  returned : final.returned = true
  column : final.regs .column = BitVec.ofNat 32 layout.inputWidth
  result : final.regs .result = rowResult ops data i
  memory : OutputStored ops data buffers i initial.globalMemory final.globalMemory
  other32 : ∀ r, r ≠ .column → r ≠ .weightValue → r ≠ .inputValue →
    r ≠ .accumulator → r ≠ .biasValue → r ≠ .result → final.regs r = initial.regs r
  other64 : ∀ r, r ≠ .weightRead → r ≠ .inputRead → final.regs64 r = initial.regs64 r
  otherPredicates : ∀ r, r ≠ .more → final.predicates r = initial.predicates r

/-- Actual concatenated-program execution, reusing the loop and suffix theorems. -/
theorem body_correct (ops : FP32.Arithmetic) (data : TensorData layout rows)
    (buffers : Buffers) (i : Fin rows) (initial : State Register) (id : Identity)
    (env : Environment) (hentry : BodyEntry layout rows buffers data i initial) :
    ∃ final, run (bodyProgram layout.inputWidth) id (bodySteps layout.inputWidth)
        initial env (some ops) = some final ∧ BodyResult ops data buffers i initial final := by
  obtain ⟨middle, hloop, hinv⟩ :=
    dotLoop_correct ops data buffers i initial id env hentry
  have hb : middle.regs64 .biasRead = elementAddress buffers .bias i.val :=
    (hinv.other64 .biasRead (by decide) (by decide)).trans hentry.biasRead
  have hy : middle.regs64 .outputWrite = elementAddress buffers .output i.val :=
    (hinv.other64 .outputWrite (by decide) (by decide)).trans hentry.outputWrite
  have hsuffix : SuffixEntry ops data buffers i middle (dotLoop layout.inputWidth).length := by
    refine ⟨?_, hinv.active, hinv.accumulator, hb, ?_, hy⟩
    · simpa [dotLoopExit, dotLoop] using hinv.pc
    · rw [hinv.memory]; exact hentry.inputs.bias i
  obtain ⟨final, hs, hr⟩ := reluSuffix_correct_at (dotLoop layout.inputWidth)
    ops data buffers i middle id env hsuffix
  have hl := run_append_of_run (dotLoop layout.inputWidth) reluSuffix id
    (dotLoopStart + dotIterationSteps * layout.inputWidth) initial middle env (some ops) hloop
  refine ⟨final, ?_, ?_⟩
  · unfold bodyProgram bodySteps
    rw [run_add, hl]
    exact hs
  · constructor
    · simpa [bodyProgram] using hr.pc
    · exact hr.returned
    · exact (hr.other32 .column (by decide) (by decide) (by decide)).trans hinv.column
    · exact hr.result
    · simpa only [hinv.memory] using hr.memory
    · intro r hc hw hx ha hb hresult
      exact (hr.other32 r hb ha hresult).trans (hinv.other32 r hc hw hx ha)
    · intro r hw hx
      rw [hr.regs64]; exact hinv.other64 r hw hx
    · intro r hmore
      rw [hr.predicates]; exact hinv.otherPredicates r hmore

passage.quote:
private theorem step_append_of_step [DecidableEq Reg]
    (program suffix : List (Instruction Reg)) (id : Identity) (s next : State Reg)
    (env : Environment) (ops : Option FP32.Arithmetic)
    (h : step program id s env ops = some next) :
    step (program ++ suffix) id s env ops = some next := by
  have hpc : s.pc < program.length := by
    by_contra hn
    have hf := List.getElem?_eq_none (l := program) (by omega : program.length ≤ s.pc)
    simp [step, hf] at h
  simpa only [step, List.getElem?_append_left hpc] using h

/-- Appending instructions cannot change an already successful prefix execution. -/
theorem run_append_of_run [DecidableEq Reg]
    (program suffix : List (Instruction Reg)) (id : Identity) (fuel : Nat)
    (s final : State Reg) (env : Environment) (ops : Option FP32.Arithmetic)
    (h : run program id fuel s env ops = some final) :
    run (program ++ suffix) id fuel s env ops = some final := by
  induction fuel generalizing s with
  | zero => simpa [run] using h
  | succ fuel ih =>
    obtain ⟨next, hs, ht⟩ := Option.bind_eq_some_iff.mp h
    have he := step_append_of_step program suffix id s next env ops hs
    simpa only [run, he, Option.bind_some] using ih next ht

def main (args : List String) : IO Unit := do
  let source ← IO.FS.readFile (args.headD "kernels/relu_layer.ptx")
  let lines := ((source.splitOn "\n").map (fun line => line.trimAscii.toString)).filter
    (fun line => !line.isEmpty && !(line.startsWith "//"))
  let normalized := "\n" ++ String.intercalate "\n" lines ++ "\n"
  unless (normalized.splitOn expectedSource).length == 2 do
    throw (IO.userError s!"Expected exactly one complete computational block:\n{expectedSource}")
  -- Artificial word arithmetic supplies independent full-size execution oracles.
  let sumOps : FP32.Arithmetic := ⟨fun w x acc => acc + w * x, fun a b => a + b⟩
  let fullInitial : State Register := { initial with
    regs64 := fun r => match r with
      | .weightRead => 0 | .inputRead => 8192 | .biasRead => 16380 | .outputWrite => 16384 | _ => 999
    globalMemory := fun a => if a.toNat < 4096 then some 2
      else if 8192 ≤ a.toNat && a.toNat < 12288 then some 3
      else if a = 16380 then some 1 else if a = 16388 then some 0x3f800000 else none }
  match run (bodyProgram layerLayout.inputWidth) ⟨0, 0⟩
      (bodySteps layerLayout.inputWidth) fullInitial Environment.empty (some sumOps) with
  | none => throw (IO.userError "Full-width body execution failed.")
  | some final =>
    unless final.pc == (bodyProgram layerLayout.inputWidth).length && final.returned &&
        final.regs .column == 1024 && final.regs .result == 6145 &&
        final.globalMemory 16384 == some 6145 && final.globalMemory 16380 == some 1 &&
        final.globalMemory 16388 == some 0x3f800000 do
      throw (IO.userError "Full-width body output/frame did not match independent oracles.")
  IO.println "Complete computational block, suffix offset, 1024-column output/frame, and exact PTX source pass."
